## Highlights

Developmental biointegration enables bioelectronics to become embedded within organoids, engineered tissues, and developing organisms, creating cyborg systems capable of long-term interaction with living tissues.

Integration of electrophysiological, molecular, and spatial measurements enables reconstruction of biological states and direct links between cellular identity and function.

Cyborg tissues are transforming regenerative medicine, disease modeling, and drug discovery by enabling biological systems to be studied as dynamic and evolving processes. Advancement toward prototypes or preclinical testing presents with ethical questions and may require new regulatory frameworks.

The convergence of embedded bioelectronics, multimodal profiling, and artificial intelligence is establishing a foundation for adaptive cyborg systems capable of biological state inference, prediction, and feedback-guided modulation.

The ethical and legal aspects of cyborg tissue systems and applications such as biocomputing require attention. Communication about the research among the broader public is needed to assure transparency and maintain trust in the science.

## Abstract

Organoids and engineered tissues have emerged as powerful models of human biology, yet their development and function are often characterized through endpoint measurements that provide only static snapshots of dynamic biological processes. Recent advances in stretchable mesh electronics, developmental biointegration, and organoid engineering have enabled the creation of cyborg tissues with embedded sensing, stimulation, and computational capabilities. This review highlights recent progress in developmental bioelectronic integration, multifunctional tissue mapping, biological state reconstruction, and artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled cyborg systems. We discuss how embedded bioelectronics can be combined with molecular and spatial profiling technologies to characterize tissue function, developmental trajectories, and biological states. These advances establish cyborg tissues as biologically integrated platforms for regenerative medicine, disease modeling, drug discovery, and adaptive biotechnology.

Adaptive biological systems

biological systems that can continuously sense, respond to, and potentially optimize their behavior through feedback-driven interactions with embedded multimodal bioelectronics and computational algorithms.

Bioelectronic medicine

a therapeutic paradigm that uses bioelectronic systems to continuously sense, interpret, and modulate biological function. Advances in embedded bioelectronics and AI are expanding the field beyond neuromodulation toward adaptive and personalized interventions guided by real-time biological state information.

Biological state

a multidimensional representation of a biological system that integrates functional, molecular, spatial, and developmental information. Biological states extend beyond physiological activity alone and provide a framework for describing tissue function, maturation, and disease progression.

Closed-loop bioelectronic system

a system that continuously acquires biological information and adapts stimulation or intervention parameters through feedback-controlled operation.

Developmental biointegration

a strategy in which bioelectronics are incorporated during tissue organogenesis or embryogenesis, allowing bioelectronics and cells to develop together and become integrated throughout the 3D tissue volume.
